1.title: Initiating a Project in Context
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Initiating a Project in Context. It covers the exam area The prince two processes. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. four point three.one carry out initiating a project: activities, inputs and outputs. Recommended roles and responsibilities. How the practices are applied. four point three.two analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, using the purpose and objectives, the practices and tailoring. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two processes (thirty percent). Exam format: an open-book scenario exam: one hundred fifty minutes, seventy marks, forty-two marks to pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Practitioner syllabus (people cert), version seven point two.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and context
1.text: Purpose, objectives and context. The initiating a project process builds solid foundations, so the organization understands the work needed to deliver the project's products before committing to significant spend. It takes place in the initiation stage, which the board authorized at the end of start-up.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and context, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and context. The figure shows this: Initiating a project: the project brief and the initiation stage plan go in, and the P I D and the next stage plan come out for the board decision to authorize the project.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and context, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and context. In plain words, the objectives are. Everyone agrees what the project is to achieve, why, how, by whom and at what cost, quality and risk. The business case is refined, and the plans and tolerances support it. The approaches and controls are set and tailored to the project. A baseline, the P I D, is ready for the board's decision to authorize the project. The process serves ensure continued business justification, learn from experience, define roles, responsibilities and relationships, manage by stages, focus on products and tailor to suit the project. Exam tip: Initiating produces the P I D; starting up produced the project brief. The P I D is the baseline the board decides on and the project is controlled against.

1.title: Activities, inputs and outputs
1.text: Activities, inputs and outputs. Activity names are given in general terms. The Official Book's wording may differ slightly, so learn what each activity achieves. Prepare the management approaches. One approach for each area: benefits, sustainability, commercial, quality, risk, issues, communication, change, digital and data. Set up the project controls. Tolerances, reporting, decision points and logs, so the project can be controlled. Plan the project. The project plan, the project product description and the stage structure, with estimates and a schedule.

1.title: Activities, inputs and outputs, continued
1.text: Activities, inputs and outputs. Refine the business case. A detailed case that uses the real costs and timescale from the plan. Assemble the P I D. One baseline document set that the board can decide on.

1.title: Activities, inputs and outputs, continued
1.text: Activities, inputs and outputs. Inputs. Authority to initiate; the project brief; the initiation stage plan; the project log and lessons from start-up; corporate standards. Outputs. The P I D; the plan for the next stage, prepared for the board; the updated project log, including the lessons log. Exam tip: The board needs both the P I D and the next stage plan to authorize the project. An approach that sends only the P I D, or only a plan for the next stage, is incomplete.

1.title: Roles and responsibilities
1.text: Roles and responsibilities. The project manager leads this process, and the board decides on the result. Learn each focus and check the Official Book's responsibility table. Executive. Accountable for the refined business case and for the justified project the board will decide on. Senior user. Accountable for the user need: acceptance criteria and how benefits will be measured. Senior supplier. Makes sure the supplier side of the plan, estimates and commercial approach is realistic. Project manager. Prepares the approaches, controls and plan; refines the case with the executive; assembles the P I D.

1.title: Roles and responsibilities, continued
1.text: Roles and responsibilities. Project assurance. Independently checks that the P I D is sound and consistent. Project support. Builds the document set, sets up the tools, filing and project log. Corporate or programme management. Provides the standards and the project tolerances the P I D must respect. Exam tip: The project manager prepares; the board owns the decision. Each board member answers for their own interest in the P I D, and assurance checks but does not approve.

1.title: How the practices are applied
1.text: How the practices are applied. Business case. Refined business case; benefits management and sustainability management approaches. Organization. Team structure, role descriptions and commercial management approach. Plans. Project plan, project product description, plan for the next stage; detail for the next stage only. Quality. Quality management approach; product descriptions for the main products; quality and product registers started. Risk. Risk management approach; risk register reviewed with owners and responses. Issues. Issue management approach, with change control, change authority and any change budget. Progress. Tolerances, reporting and controls; digital and data management approach; lessons log. Exam tip: Every practice has a product in the P I D, and the plans and tolerances must agree with the business case. If the plan costs more than the benefits justify, the case must be revisited, not hidden.

1.title: Judging the process
1.text: Judging the process. A P I D that is the baseline for decisions and control. A P I D written, filed and never used or updated (business justification). Approaches tailored and proportionate. A full template copied without thought, or approaches missing (tailor). Plans and tolerances consistent with the business case. Cost above what the benefits justify, or tolerances wider than the corporate limits (business justification). A product-based plan with acceptance criteria. An activity list with no project product description (focus on products).

1.title: Judging the process, continued
1.text: Judging the process. Detail for the next stage, outline for later ones. Every stage planned in detail months ahead (manage by stages). A business case refined with real costs and benefit owners. The brief's case copied unchanged (business justification). Roles and stakeholders agreed and described. Unclear roles; key stakeholders missing from the communication approach (define roles). Lessons from start-up used. Earlier lessons ignored (learn from experience).

2.title: Judging the process, continued
2.text: Judging the process. Tailoring makes the P I D proportionate, not smaller than the need. Small project. A short P I D; approaches as brief paragraphs or a reference to organization standards. Agile or hybrid delivery. The P I D records iteration length, how the backlog is controlled and how tolerances apply to each time-box. Large or multi-supplier project. Separate, formal approach documents; a detailed commercial management approach; links to the programme. Sustainability, digital and data concerns. Targets and data protection set out in the approaches. Exam tip: Judge a P I D by whether it is fit to decide on, not by its length. A two-page P I D can be effective; a hundred pages that nobody reads is not.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Sam Okafor's P I D for Project Harbor plans all four stages in full detail, including the rollout stage, to give the board confidence. Was this an appropriate action, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: No, because later stages should be outlined, with detail kept for the stage ahead. The planning horizon limits reliable detail to the next stage, while the P I D still holds an outline project plan.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. While refining the business case for Project Harbor, Sam finds that the plan costs five hundred thirty thousand, not the four hundred eighty thousand in the project brief. What should Sam do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Update the business case with the higher cost and tell the executive before the decision. The business case must be refined with real costs and the executive must know before the decision, in line with continued business justification.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Sam wants to confirm that the acceptance criteria in Project Harbor's project product description will give permit users what they need. Who should confirm this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The senior user, Tomas Reyes. The senior user is accountable for the user need and for how well the products meet it.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Which management product records how the benefits of Project Harbor will be measured, when, and by whom? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The benefits management approach in the P I D. The benefits management approach covers how and when benefits are measured and who is responsible, while the other products cover contracts, quality and the product itself.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Wei Chen's team will deliver Project Harbor in iterations. Sam records in the P I D the iteration length, how the backlog is controlled and how tolerances apply to each time-box. Was this an appropriate action, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Yes, because initiating tailors the approaches to the delivery method and shows control. Tailoring decisions are recorded in the P I D so the board sees how the project will be controlled, and the business case and plan are still needed.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Sam has assembled the P I D for Project Harbor and Aisha Bello has reviewed it. What should Sam do next? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Give the P I D and the next stage plan to the board so it can decide on the project. The board authorizes the project on the P I D and the next stage plan, and assurance review is a check, not an authorization.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of initiating a project? Answer: To build solid foundations so the organization understands the work needed before committing to significant spend. Question two. What is the main output of initiating a project? Answer: The project initiation documentation (P I D). Question three. Name two activities of initiating in general terms. Answer: Preparing the management approaches, setting up the project controls, planning the project, refining the business case, or assembling the P I D.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which two products from start-up are the inputs that authorize this process? Answer: The project brief and the initiation stage plan. Question five. Who decides whether to authorize the project after initiating? Answer: The project board. Question six. Where are tailoring decisions recorded? Answer: In the P I D.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Purpose: solid foundations before significant spend. Inputs: project brief, initiation stage plan, project log, lessons. Outputs: the P I D and the next stage plan. Activities: approaches, controls, project plan, refined case, assemble the P I D. Roles: project manager prepares; executive, senior user and senior supplier answer for their interest. Judging: baseline used, proportionate approaches, plans and tolerances match the case. Tailoring: proportionate P I D; record how the delivery method is controlled.
